feature1.prompt: Feature 1: Class methods from nested classes are currently not correctly handled when used as Field.default. In the provided model, the 'capabilities' field default is set to a class method from the nested class Capability. This leads to an incorrect migration where the default is recorded as 'appname.models.Capability.default' instead of the correct 'appname.models.Profile.Capability.default'. The fix requires updating the serialization logic so that the nested class method is referenced using its fully qualified name, ensuring that the migration is generated without errors.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature addresses the core bug in the serialization process. Developers should update the serializer so that it uses the qualified name of a nested class when computing the default value. In particular, the code needs to replace the use of the __name__ attribute with __qualname__ to construct the proper migration string. The implementation should be verified against existing tests that are expected to pass both before and after the fix.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/db/migrations/serializer.py. Locate the serialize method where the return statement is built. Specifically, update the line that formats the output string by replacing 'klass.__name__' with 'klass.__qualname__'. This change is crucial to ensure that nested class methods are properly identified during migration serialization.

feature2.prompt: Feature 2: The migration process fails because the default value for the 'capabilities' field in the model is not being correctly referenced. The problem arises when a class method from a nested class is used as the default, resulting in the migration receiving the wrong method path ('appname.models.Capability.default') instead of the proper 'appname.models.Profile.Capability.default'. This discrepancy leads to an error during migration execution. The intended behavior is that the migration should capture the correct fully qualified name so that the field default is applied without issues.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature focuses on validating the fix by adding a verification for the correct serialization of nested class methods. Developers should implement a new test that specifically checks that the migration default is generated with the fully qualified name. The added test must assert that the output matches the expected corrected value, ensuring that the error encountered during migration no longer occurs. Attention should be paid to the formatting of the serialized string and the import statement it produces.
feature2.entrypoint: File: tests/migrations/test_writer.py. Introduce a new test method to verify that a nested class method is correctly serialized for use as Field.default. The new test should confirm that when the method from the nested class is passed, the resulting serialization string correctly reflects the nested structure with its fully qualified name. This test serves as a guard against regression and confirms the validity of the fix implemented in the serializer.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features modify and interact with the migration serialization logic and its corresponding tests. The serializer in django/db/migrations/serializer.py and the test suite in tests/migrations/test_writer.py are common points of integration.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature 1 provides the core fix by changing the serialization of nested class methods, while Feature 2 adds a test to verify the corrected behavior. Once the serializer is updated, the new test must be executed to ensure that the fix behaves as expected. There is a dependency between the features, as the test in Feature 2 directly validates the changes made in Feature 1.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers enforcing the serializer fix and those writing the new test case must coordinate on the expected serialized output format. Regular communication is needed to confirm that the changes in the serializer are correctly reflected in the test outcomes. Integration meetings or code reviews should emphasize the handling of nested class method references to avoid regression issues.
